title: Redwood PLG quickstart discovery - Kestrel AI
summary: Initial discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Customer wants fast time-to-first-token, understanding of free credits/quickstart, and evaluation of hosted vs dedicated vs private for a recommendation system PoC. Security (SOC2, SSO, VPC) and benchmarking latency/cost are key blockers. Agreed next steps: send quickstart guide + free credits instructions, share security docs, and set a technical deep dive to scope a small benchmark pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) evaluation
Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching/quantization
Security controls: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. Quick intros?
[00:08] Sam (Kestrel CTO): Sam here, CTO. Maya is our eng manager, Liam does infra. We have a quick agenda, we want to understand how fast we can get up and running with Redwood API and which deployment makes sense for us — hosted for now but potentially dedicated or private later.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, I'm Priya, SE on the platform. We'll walk through quickstart, free credits, and how to run a small latency/cost benchmark. Also happy to dig into security — VPC, KMS, SOC2.
[00:40] Maya (Kestrel): Quick thing up front: our timeline is 6–8 weeks for a PoC. We need to show a recommendation model in a staging environment and then maybe production. Latency target is p95 < 120ms for 256-token responses; cost needs to be within our per-user budget.
[01:10] Jordan: Great. For PLG quickstart folks we typically get them first token in minutes — sign up, API key, run curl or SDK example. We give free credits that cover a small benchmark. That's usually enough to validate time-to-first-token and early integration.
[01:35] Liam (SRE): When you say "hosted" what are the data retention / logs? We can't ship PII to third parties at first.
[01:45] Priya: Good question. Hosted API defaults to ephemeral logs for request debugging; we have retention settings, and for regulated data we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and data isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control — both support KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:10] Sam: What's the onboarding friction for dedicated? We don't want 90‑day procurement cycles.
[02:20] Jordan: Dedicated can be fast for mid-market if you sign a reserved capacity contract; for PLG evaluation you can start hosted with quickstart and then convert to dedicated. The quickstart to production path is one of our focus points — same API surface.
[02:40] Maya: How do you handle SSO and RBAC? We have strict access policies.
[02:50] Priya: SSO/SAML provisioning is available for Dedicated and Private; for hosted you can use org-level API keys and team controls in the console. RBAC, audit logs, and per-route model access are supported on Dedicated/Private for enterprise tiers.
[03:20] Jordan: To make this concrete — we can give you a free credits pack to run a short benchmark (we'll send a docker script or curl/SDK steps). Typical script exercises tokens at different sequence lengths and a steady QPS to get p95 latency and cost numbers.
[03:45] Sam: That sounds useful. What about model selection — do we pull open models or Redwood-managed weights? We want to try a smaller quantized model first for cost.
[03:55] Priya: You can pick from our model catalog — we host curated open models and also have Redwood-verified profiles. For evaluation we often recommend a 4‑bit quantized variant to test cost/latency before trying larger variants. Batching and prefix caching options also help.
[04:25] Liam: Is there a way to measure per-token cost breakdown and attribute cost to routes/users?
[04:35] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards; we can show you cost by API key so you can attribute to teams or features.
[04:50] Maya: Any hard limits on rate or concurrency during quickstart? We want to simulate 100 concurrent users.
[04:58] Priya: For hosted quickstarts we provide a reasonable quota. If you need sustained 100 concurrent users, we can either temporarily bump quotas or run the benchmark against a Dedicated trial environment. We also recommend using our batching settings to model cost.
[05:20] Sam: Security docs — SOC2, ISO, network diagrams, pen test?
[05:27] Jordan: We'll share a security packet: SOC2 report, ISO attestation summary, network architecture for Dedicated/Private, and our pen test recs. I'll attach those after the call.
[05:40] Maya: Performance — your 120ms p95 for 256 tokens, is that typical?
[05:48] Priya: It depends on model and hardware. For a quantized 7B on midspec GPUs we often see p95 around 60–150ms with good batching. For hosted we publish latency profiles per model.
[06:10] Sam: Cost ballpark? Per 1M tokens?
[06:15] Jordan: For open models on hosted, cost varies by model and quantization — range is wide. We'll include model-and-sequence-length examples in the pricing doc. The Optimize toolkit can suggest batching and quantization profiles to reduce cost.
[06:35] Liam: Networking — can Dedicated be placed in our cloud region and support VPC peering?
[06:42] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports customer-managed networking and on-prem installs if needed. KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated.
[06:58] Sam: Any customer references using Redwood for a recommendations stack?
[07:04] Jordan: We have a few e-commerce and recommendation customers; I'll share anonymized case studies and a short benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:15] Maya: About error handling — do you stream errors or have retries/backoff?
[07:22] Priya: Streaming is supported; we also have built-in retry guidance and trace hooks for observability. The Console surfaces errors per-model and per-route.
[07:40] Jordan: Ok let's outline a pilot: steps are 1) send quickstart + credits, 2) customer runs benchmark script against hosted, 3) we review results and recommend hosted vs dedicated. If results show high concurrency needs or data residency concerns, we scope Dedicated/Private.
[08:05] Sam: Sounds doable. For the benchmark, we want p95 latency, mean latency, and cost per request; success criteria: p95 < 120ms and cost <$0.02 per end-user request (approx).
[08:22] Priya: We'll add those metrics to the script and the scoring sheet. Any particular models you want to test?
[08:30] Sam: Start with a quantized 7B and a 13B baseline if time permits.
[08:36] Jordan: Noted. I'll include both model profiles in the benchmark.
[08:45] Maya: Questions about data retention again — for hosted, if we opt to redact PII can that be done automatically?
[08:55] Priya: We have policy-based redaction guidance. For strict PII controls, Dedicated or Private is recommended because you control logs and retention. Hosted has tooling but not full data residency guarantees.
[09:15] Liam: On SLA, what uptime guarantees apply to hosted vs dedicated?
[09:22] Jordan: Hosted has best-effort availability for PLG tiers; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of the reserved capacity contract. Private can be contractually defined depending on deployment.
[09:40] Sam: Integration questions — we use Python microservices. Are there SDKs?
[09:45] Priya: Yes, SDKs for Python, Node, and a simple REST curl example. The quickstart repo includes sample microservice code for token streaming and retry logic.
[10:05] Jordan: Let's also talk about costs if you convert to Dedicated — typically you sign a monthly commit and can negotiate burst capacity. We'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[10:18] Maya: How long to switch from hosted to Dedicated without code changes?
[10:24] Priya: Usually it's config-only; same API endpoint semantics and SDKs. You can pin model versions and rollout via our Console.
[10:40] Sam: One last item — compliance team will request dataflow diagrams and encryption-at-rest details.
[10:47] Jordan: We'll include that in the security packet.
[11:00] Jordan: Ok, I'll summarise next steps now. Anything else?
[11:08] Maya: Not for now.
[11:09] Liam: No.
[11:12] Sam: Good, thanks.
[11:15] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the quickstart, credits, security docs, and propose a timeslot for the deep technical dive next week.
[11:25] End of recording (call ~48 minutes).
